commit_subject: fix: fail closed on unrounded ACA percentages
description: 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) requires the interpolated percentage rounded to the nearest 0.01 percentage point; that regulation is NOT in the pinned corpus, so instead of emitting an unrounded chain, EVERY public output carrying the operative percentage/contribution/assistance chain is gated on an on-grid validity judgment — off-grid ratios fail closed to zero/not_holds

triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The pre-fix validity judgment held (fail-open) for every household-income/FPL ratio, so for ratios whose 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) linear interpolation lands off the 0.01-percentage-point grid the module exported an annual premium tax credit computed from a raw unrounded applicable percentage, a rate that disagrees with the rounded percentage 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) requires.
triage.triage_notes: Read the whole diff plus pre-fix (46ddf937a) and post-fix module bodies; also resolved us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-25 through the pinned corpus, which confirms the new parameter's proof excerpt verbatim ('the Applicable Percentage Table for purposes of § 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g) is') and that the 2026 table endpoints (2.10/3.14/4.19/6.60/8.44/9.96%) are stated to 0.01 percentage point, supporting the 0.0001 grid increment. 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g) itself is NOT in the pinned corpus (the module says the resolver finds no provision for it), so the rounding requirement itself could not be read directly — evidence for it is the commit/PR text plus the rev proc's cross-reference. Kind is genuinely contestable: I chose polarity_or_logic because the commit subject ('fail closed on unrounded ACA percentages') and PR body ('off-grid ratios fail closed to zero/not_holds') name the fail-open→fail-closed change, the taxonomy lists fail-open vs fail-closed under polarity_or_logic, and the decisive diff is an added and-clause in a boolean Judgment formula. The strong alternative is unrepresented_clause: the underlying disagreement with the source is the missing 1.36B-3(g) rounding operation, which the pre-fix module disclosed only as a deferred output ('Required fixtures use table endpoints, constant bands, or an exact midpoint, so this missing operation does not change their rates') while still exporting an operative unrounded chain; note the fix does not add the rounding, it narrows the domain. Alternative quotable line from inside the module diff (quote_source module_comment): 'The pinned corpus resolver finds no provision for 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g), so this module does not claim to compute the general rounded rate.' Scope caveat: the PR body describes head ce08e342a and claims EVERY public output is gated, but at THIS commit only rules[aca_ptc_annual_premium_tax_credit] consumes the validity judgment; the public intermediates were gated in follow-up 2d032aa87 ('fix: gate ACA PTC public arithmetic off grid') and the guard expression was restructured in 3a7b27612 ('fix: express ACA PTC grid guard as judgment logic'), both same-day commits in PR #1002. The commit also touched only prose/deferral metadata otherwise (module summary, deferred_outputs reason plus new source_values, and the rule's `source` string) — no other formula, parameter, effective date, input, output, or entity changed. The PR has no reviews or review comments in the bundle.
triage.verifier_justification: Both cited corpus sources are silent on rounding: the pinned 26 USC 36B text states only that the applicable percentage "shall increase, on a sliding scale in a linear manner, from the initial premium percentage to the final premium percentage", and Rev. Proc. 2025-25 contains zero occurrences of "round"/"nearest"/"hundredth" — so the pre-fix raw linear interpolation matched the cited source text exactly, and the module had already declared the rounded rate a deferred output. The fix does not encode the source rule it invokes; by its own words the regulation is un-ingested ("The pinned corpus resolver finds no provision for 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g)"), the deferral stays in place, and the module instead refuses to answer off-grid, which its own companion documents as moving the exported credit from $5,209.9668 (raw rate, 66 cents from the lawful $5,209.3095) to $0 — further from the lawful amount, not closer. That is a provenance/conservatism policy choice about what the module may claim, not an encoded meaning corrected against a cited source, so neither polarity_or_logic nor any fidelity kind fits cleanly. Separately, the quoted PR-body evidence describes the merged head, not this commit: "EVERY public output" only became gated two commits later in 2d032aa87 "fix: gate ACA PTC public arithmetic off grid", which had to inline the interpolation to undo the self-referential `hash: sha256:local` import this commit introduced.
triage.verifier_quote: +    source: Guard-only 0.01-percentage-point increment required by un-ingested 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g); not a general rounded-rate output
triage.verifier_notes:
Strongest counterargument to my verdict (a reviewer may prefer "unclear"): the pre-fix module did export a PTC amount that disagrees with real-world law, and the framework lists "fail-open vs fail-closed" under polarity_or_logic. But the missing thing is the rounding operation of 26 CFR 1.36B-3(g), which is still unrepresented after the fix — the fix quarantines the gap rather than curing it — so if anyone insists on a fidelity label, unrepresented_clause fits the underlying gap better than polarity_or_logic, and neither is satisfied by this diff.

Evidence chain, all read-only: (1) pinned corpus us/statute/26/36B (release us-rulespec-2026-07-24-snap-cms-pit-union, corpus commit 0fd35bfbda) contains no rounding language for 36B(b)(3)(A)(i); us/guidance/irs/rev-proc-2025-25 has 0 hits for round/nearest/hundredth/0.01 and mentions § 1.36B-3 only in its header cross-reference line — which is also the excerpt the new guard parameter's proof atom leans on ("the Applicable Percentage Table for purposes of § 36B(b)(3)(A)(i) and § 1.36B-3(g) is"). (2) Pre-fix 46ddf937a0 already deferred us:regulations/26-cfr/1.36B-3/g#rounded_applicable_percentage and already gated aca_ptc_annual_premium_tax_credit on aca_ptc_full_year_runtime_inputs_valid; the only computational change in this commit is one added conjunct plus the 0.0001 grid parameter. (3) The companion case added here, off-grid-210fpl-fails-closed-pending-regulatory-rounding, states the lawful rounded chain ($2,290.6905 contribution, $5,209.3095 credit), the raw-rate credit ($5,209.9668) and the new output ($0).

Context a reviewer should weigh: us/policies/aca/ptc_pipeline.yaml was created two days earlier in the same PR (#1002) at 72058b2b0 and iterated five times (44a871f06, 52224b0513, 8e72ccd28, 2d032aa87, 3a7b27612). This candidate is an intermediate blind-review round on unmerged new code, not a fix to a shipped module, and the next two commits had to rework the very formula it added (inlining the interpolation to break the cycle it created, then re-expressing the guard "as judgment logic").
